senses.gloss: To make a rule, a restriction, or a budget stricter and less generous.
examples: The city *tightened* the rules on short-term rentals.
Congress may *tighten* the restrictions again next year.
Security has been *tightened* at every airport in the country.

senses.gloss: To choose the right moment for something to happen.
examples: They *timed* the announcement to land right before the holidays.
If you *time* it well, you can catch the early train.
The whole campaign was badly *timed*.

senses.gloss: To lean to one side or fall over, or to make something do that.
examples: Don't *tip* your chair back like that.
He *tipped* the bucket and poured the water into the sink.
The canoe was *tipping* dangerously in the wind.

senses.gloss: To be able to take a drug, a food, or hard conditions without being harmed.
examples: Some patients cannot *tolerate* this antibiotic.
She *tolerated* the first round of treatment better than her doctors expected.
These shrubs are known for *tolerating* drought and poor soil.

senses.gloss: To be greater than an amount, or to stand in first place on a list.
examples: No one expected the sequel to *top* the original.
Sales *topped* a million dollars last quarter.
The song has *topped* the charts for six straight weeks.

senses.gloss: To remove a leader or a government from power.
examples: The protests *toppled* the government in a matter of weeks.
No one believed a strike could *topple* a president.
Three regimes in the region have been *toppled* since 2011.

senses.gloss: To add up to a particular amount.
examples: The repairs *totaled* almost four thousand dollars.
Her medical bills *total* more than she earns in a year.
Donations have *totaled* over a million dollars since May.

senses.gloss: To travel from city to city giving performances.
examples: The band *tours* every summer.
They *toured* Europe with a new drummer.
She is *touring* the country with her one-woman show.

senses.gloss: To copy a picture by drawing over its lines through thin paper.
senses.ru: обводить, обвести (по контуру); перерисовывать через кальку
examples: Kids love to *trace* the letters with a pencil.
He *traced* the map onto a sheet of tissue paper.
She was *tracing* the outline of a leaf for her art class.

senses.gloss: To carry dirt, snow, or water into a place on the bottom of your shoes.
examples: Don't *track* mud through the kitchen!
The dog *tracked* wet leaves all over the carpet.
Someone has *tracked* snow into the hallway again.

senses.gloss: To buy and sell stocks, currency, or commodities on a market.
examples: He *trades* bonds for a hedge fund.
The stock *traded* below ten dollars all week.
Oil has been *trading* near record highs.

senses.gloss: To be losing in a game, a race, or an election.
examples: The Celtics *trailed* by twelve at halftime.
She *trails* the front-runner by six points in the polls.
They have *trailed* all season and still made the playoffs.

senses.gloss: To practice and exercise in order to get ready for a sport or a physical test.
examples: He *trains* six days a week.
She *trained* for two years before her first marathon.
They have been *training* at altitude since March.

senses.gloss: To pass a disease from one person or animal to another.
examples: Mosquitoes *transmit* the virus to humans.
The infection was *transmitted* through contaminated water.
Masks reduce the risk of *transmitting* the flu at work.

senses.gloss: To dig up a plant and put it in the ground somewhere else.
examples: Wait until fall to *transplant* the roses.
We *transplanted* the seedlings into bigger pots.
The tomatoes are ready to be *transplanted* outside.

senses.gloss: To make someone feel that they are in a different place or time.
examples: The smell of pine *transports* me back to my grandmother's kitchen.
The novel *transported* her to nineteenth-century Paris.
For two hours we were *transported* to another world.

senses.gloss: To switch the position of two letters, numbers, or words, usually by mistake.
examples: It is easy to *transpose* two digits when you copy a long number.
The clerk *transposed* the last two figures of my account.
Someone had *transposed* the first and last names on the form.

senses.gloss: To throw something away.
examples: Just *trash* those old magazines.
I *trashed* the whole first draft and started over.
Every receipt from the trip has already been *trashed*.

senses.gloss: To criticize someone or something harshly in public.
examples: Critics *trashed* the movie the day it opened.
Don't *trash* your old company in a job interview.
He has been *trashing* his opponent on every talk show.

senses.gloss: To behave toward someone or something in a particular way.
examples: They *treat* their employees well.
He *treated* her like a stranger.
I don't like being *treated* as a child.

senses.gloss: To give medical care to a person or an illness.
examples: Doctors *treat* the infection with antibiotics.
Paramedics *treated* her at the scene.
He is being *treated* for a broken wrist.

senses.gloss: To put a chemical on something in order to protect it or change it.
examples: We *treat* the deck every other spring.
They *treated* the water before pumping it into town.
The lumber has been *treated* to resist rot.

senses.gloss: To decorate something, especially along its edges.
examples: We *trim* the tree the day after Thanksgiving.
She *trimmed* the collar with red ribbon.
The stockings were *trimmed* with white fur.

senses.gloss: To set off a switch, an alarm, or a circuit breaker, usually by accident.
examples: The space heater *trips* the breaker every time.
A cat *tripped* the motion sensor at three in the morning.
The alarm was *tripped* by a gust of wind.

senses.gloss: Of a person, to move along quickly with short steps.
examples: She *trotted* over to say hello.
The little boy *trots* after his sister everywhere she goes.
He came *trotting* up the driveway, out of breath.

senses.gloss: To be more important than something else and so outweigh it.
examples: Safety concerns *trump* cost every time.
Her experience *trumped* his connections.
In this office, speed has always *trumped* polish.

senses.gloss: To make an effort to do something.
examples: I'll *try* to be there by six.
She *tried* three times before the door opened.
He has been *trying* to reach you all morning.

senses.gloss: To use or taste something in order to find out whether it is good or whether it works.
examples: You should *try* the soup — it's incredible.
We *tried* a new route to avoid the traffic.
Have you ever *tried* skiing?

senses.gloss: To examine a case, or the person accused, in a court of law.
examples: They plan to *try* the two men separately.
The judge *tried* the case without a jury.
He will be *tried* in federal court next spring.

senses.gloss: To fall quickly and sharply in value.
examples: Stocks *tumbled* after the announcement.
If rates rise again, the market could *tumble*.
Home prices have *tumbled* since the spring.

senses.gloss: To become something different, especially in color, taste, or condition.
examples: The leaves *turn* red in October.
The milk *turned* sour overnight.
His face had *turned* white before he said a word.

senses.gloss: To reach a particular age or hour.
examples: She *turns* thirty in June.
He *turned* sixty last week.
It had just *turned* midnight when the phone rang.

senses.gloss: To hurt a joint by turning it the wrong way.
examples: I *twisted* my ankle on the stairs.
Don't *twist* your knee getting out of the car.
He has *twisted* the same wrist twice this season.

senses.gloss: To change the meaning of what someone said in an unfair way.
examples: Stop *twisting* my words.
The article *twisted* everything she said.
His quote had been *twisted* by the time it reached print.

senses.gloss: To make clear that something is important.
examples: The accident *underlines* the need for better lighting.
Her resignation *underlined* how bad things had gotten.
The report has *underlined* the risks of waiting.

senses.gloss: To develop or happen gradually over a period of time.
examples: The scandal *unfolded* over several months.
We watched the story *unfold* on live television.
Events were still *unfolding* when we went to press.

senses.gloss: To examine a complicated idea or statement piece by piece.
examples: Let's *unpack* that argument piece by piece.
The professor *unpacked* the theory over two lectures.
She spent the whole hour *unpacking* one sentence from the ruling.

senses.gloss: To solve or explain something mysterious or complicated.
examples: It took investigators years to *unravel* the fraud.
Researchers *unraveled* the cause of the outbreak.
The mystery has never been fully *unraveled*.

senses.gloss: To fall apart or begin to fail.
examples: The deal *unraveled* at the last minute.
His life began to *unravel* after the injury.
Their coalition has been *unraveling* since the election.

senses.gloss: To open a compressed computer file and take the files out of it.
examples: You have to *unzip* the folder before you run the installer.
I *unzipped* the file and found three photos inside.
The attachment has already been *unzipped*.

senses.gloss: To move a passenger or a guest to a better seat or room.
senses.ru: повышать класс (места, номера), пересадить в лучший класс
examples: They *upgraded* us to business class for free.
Ask at the desk whether they can *upgrade* your room.
We were *upgraded* because the hotel had overbooked.
